introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section 1 is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section 2 in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section 2 answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Distinguish between an intrinsic semiconductor and an extrinsic semiconductor. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- An **intrinsic semiconductor** is a **pure** semiconductor (pure silicon or germanium) with no impurity added: its charge carriers are only the electrons freed from the bonds and the same number of holes they leave behind.
- An **extrinsic semiconductor** is a semiconductor to which a **small amount of a suitable impurity has been added (doped)** to increase its conductivity; it is n-type (mainly electrons) or p-type (mainly holes).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain how the conductivity of a semiconductor is affected by:

(i) doping. *[2 marks]*

(ii) an increase in temperature. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Doping** adds atoms of an impurity: a **pentavalent** atom (for example phosphorus, 5 outer electrons) gives **extra free electrons** (n-type); a **trivalent** atom (for example boron, 3 outer electrons) creates **holes** (p-type). The number of charge carriers increases a great deal, so the **conductivity increases**.

(ii) When the temperature rises, more electrons gain enough energy to break away from their covalent bonds, which creates more free electrons and more holes (electron-hole pairs). There are more charge carriers, so the **conductivity increases** (the resistance falls), unlike a metal whose resistance increases when it is heated.
